Classify two variables for a bivariate map

Source: R/bivariate.R
bi_class.Rd

bi_class() bins two numeric columns into dim classes each and adds one column holding the pair of classes as "x-y" ("1-1" is low on both, "3-3" high on both at dim = 3). Map a fill to that column and add scale_fill_bivariate() to colour it with a bivariate palette and draw the 2-D legend. The design follows the biscale package's bi_class().

Usage

bi_class(data, x, y, dim = 3, style = "quantile", name = "bi_class")

Arguments

data

A data frame or sf object.

x, y

The two numeric variables (bare column names). x runs along the legend's horizontal axis, y up its vertical one.

dim

Classes per variable: 2, 3 (default) or 4.

style

How to choose the class breaks: "quantile" (default), "equal", "pretty", or any classInt::classIntervals() style (needs the classInt package) — the same styles as scale_fill_binned().

name

Name of the new column (default "bi_class").

Value

data with a factor column name whose levels are all dim^2 classes in order. Rows where x or y is missing get NA.

Details

Classes are computed over the whole table, so a faceted map shares one set of breaks across its panels. bi_class() works on a plain data frame or an sf table (the geometry is kept). It records the two variable names on the new column, which scale_fill_bivariate() uses as the legend's axis titles when you don't give your own.

See also

scale_fill_bivariate(), bi_pal()

Other bivariate: bi_pal(), guide_bivariate(), scale_fill_bivariate()

Examples

d <- bi_class(mtcars, hp, wt)
table(d$bi_class)
#> 
#> 1-1 2-1 3-1 1-2 2-2 3-2 1-3 2-3 3-3 
#>   8   2   1   3   5   2   0   1  10
